title: A smaller edit stops a reasoning model from looping
summary: Nathan Barry used linear programming to find a sparse weight edit that reduces repetitive reasoning loops in Qwen3.5-0.8B. The edit changed about 16,000 weights versus 130,000 for an earlier agent-designed edit and scored 51.7% versus 50.9% on MATH-500 in Barry’s comparison. A fixed activation-steering vector recovered most of the gain, and the study covered one model and one failure mode.

title: A Transformer teaches a Mamba model
summary: Apple researchers transferred knowledge from a pretrained Transformer to a Mamba model through an intermediate model with linearized attention. The resulting model uses no attention blocks and reached a perplexity of 14.01, close to the Pythia-1B teacher’s 13.86. The remaining gaps were more pronounced on tasks that require recalling information from the prompt.

title: Ginux moves its Linux compatibility layer into userspace
summary: Ginux runs as a Linux process that intercepts system calls from managed programs and emulates, mediates, or denies them according to a versioned configuration. The project reports that a pinned Rocky Linux 10 instance can boot to multi-user mode, accept a console login, install updates, and shut down cleanly. Its effectiveness as a containment boundary for AI agents remains under test.

title: An agent that can resume after a crash
summary: A stock-replenishment prototype uses durable execution to preserve an agent’s progress while it waits for human approval. The workflow records model decisions and tool results, then replays the log after a crash to rebuild state without repeating completed steps. External writes still need stable idempotency keys to prevent duplicate purchase orders.

title: Relighting a photograph with editable 3D lights
summary: This resurfaced SIGGRAPH 2025 paper lets users add point lights, spotlights, or environmental illumination to a single photograph. The system estimates a 3D mesh, path-traces the new lighting, and uses a neural renderer to produce the final image. The initial render depends on geometry inferred from just one view.
